definition: Training with a small labeled set plus a large unlabeled set, using techniques like pseudo-labeling or consistency regularization to exploit the unlabeled portion.
details: Training with a small labeled set plus a large unlabeled set, using techniques like pseudo-labeling or consistency regularization to exploit the unlabeled portion.

explainer.lead: Semi-supervised learning trains on a small labeled set plus a large unlabeled set. It matters where labels are expensive but raw data is abundant.

tiers.eli5: You learn from a few labelled examples and a big pile of unlabelled ones, instead of needing everything labelled.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use pseudo-labeling or consistency regularization to exploit the unlabeled portion. A pitfall is that noisy pseudo-labels can reinforce the model's own mistakes.
tiers.paperLevel: Training with a small labeled set plus a large unlabeled set, using techniques such as pseudo-labeling or consistency regularization to exploit the unlabeled portion.

explainer.example: A classifier is trained on a few hundred labeled images and many thousands of unlabeled ones, with confident predictions on the unlabeled data used as extra training signal.
